changes: Kept the original fiscal-year start at 1993 and extended the end from 1998 through requested FY2003. The pooled means and balanced CONMKT support panel now use FY1993–FY2003; FY1992 remains available as the sales-growth base and the 1986+ return anchor history remains for the seven RET_t through RET_t−6 terms.

Expanded current-source filters to the requested fiscal/calendar endpoint. The SAS source-date cap is 31DEC2004 to allow FY2003 DATADATEs in calendar 2004; this is a filter bound, not a claim of observed coverage. The native build reports actual fiscal and CRSP dates by year.

Extended the market-model monthly return window to 1993–2003 while retaining its 24-month minimum. Kept the accepted S&P rating field screen through 31AUG1998 as the original fixed pre-1998 field-policy cutoff.

Retained the accepted SAS-to-Stata construction, balance rules, variable formulas, firm/time effects, cross-sectional OLS with intercept, robust variance, model terms, and missing-value handling. Added period support fields and computed original/added contributions on each fitted Stata e(sample); the counts are firm-level cross-sectional rows and may overlap across periods because each row contains pooled measures.

The native pooled build observed FY2003 Compustat DATADATEs through 2004-05-31, FY2003 BTM market prices through 2004-05-28, CRSP.MSF dates through 2004-12-31, and monthly CRSP index dates in every calendar year 1993–2003. The latest contributing fit period is FY2003 for both scopes.
limitations: Exact author-era 1998 Compustat/CRSP vintages and historical link policies are not established by current local files.

The paper does not specify exact book-to-market components, fiscal-year return compounding/alignment, the standard-deviation divisor, or minimum available-year rules for accounting means; the accepted construction retains its documented best-effort choices.

The paper describes fixed effects and cross-sectional regressions but does not name the underlying estimators. The accepted build uses PROC GLM least-squares means for CONMKT and direct OLS with robust standard errors in Stata; Stata p-values are two-sided while the paper reports one-sided tests where predicted.

SPLTICRM is used as a best-effort local long-term issuer rating field and eligibility remains limited to records dated through 31AUG1998, as in the accepted code; this is not a later-period rating screen.
Compustat DP includes depreciation and amortization and is used for the CONACC numerator; XDP is a diagnostic, not a proven paper-equivalent field.

The accepted CCM construction includes provider-documented LC and LU primary links and audited ordinary-common share classes; LU equivalence is unresolved, and BTM dates with unresolved company mappings remain missing.

The original accepted Stata tables have N=140 complete-case regression rows, below the paper/sample-record counts of 704 CONMKT and 632 CONACC firms. This predecessor discrepancy is preserved; the extended run is compared with the saved N=140 tables.
